UK headline APRs are "representative" — only 51% of borrowers actually receive the advertised rate. You'll see the true rate only after a formal application. Use eligibility checkers first (soft search, no credit impact) to avoid wasted hard pulls.

When a Personal Loan Wins vs Credit Cards

  • Carrying a balance: If you've had a credit card balance for 3+ months, a 7.9% personal loan beats a 24.9% credit card APR by a huge margin.
  • Fixed payoff date: Loan amortisation forces discipline. Credit card minimums can keep balances alive for decades.
  • Predictable budgeting: The fixed monthly payment is easier to plan around than fluctuating card minimums.

For short-term float (1-3 months) on a card you'll repay in full, the rewards beat any loan. For anything longer, switch to a loan.

Section 75 Consumer Credit Act Protection

For credit card purchases between £100 and £30,000, Section 75 makes the card issuer jointly liable with the retailer if something goes wrong. Personal loans don't offer this — so for high-risk purchases (overseas flights, custom goods, expensive electronics), use a credit card and pay it off with the loan if you must, rather than using the loan directly.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the calculator include arrangement fees?
No — this shows the payment based on interest rate and principal only. Some UK lenders charge arrangement fees (1-3% of loan amount); always compare APRs (which legally include fees) rather than interest rates alone.
Can I overpay or settle early?
Most UK personal loans allow overpayment, but you'll pay interest up to the settlement date plus potentially a small "early settlement charge" (capped by the Consumer Credit Act at 1-2 months' interest on the settled amount). Check your specific T&Cs.
Soft search vs hard search?
Eligibility checkers use soft searches — they don't affect your credit score. Formal applications use hard searches — visible to other lenders for 12 months, mild score impact for 3-6 months. Always start with soft search comparison tools (MSE, ClearScore, Experian) before formal applications.
UK credit score above 999 means what?
The three UK credit reference agencies use different scales (Experian out of 999, Equifax 0-1000, TransUnion 0-710). The score itself doesn't matter — what matters is which "tier" you fall into. Lenders use their own internal scoring, not the consumer-facing score.
